title: NeuroFilter: Activation-Based Guardrails for Privacy-Conscious LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2601.14660v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Agentic Large Language Models (LLMs) are models able to reason, plan, and execute tools over unstructured data. These abilities enable transformative applications in domains spanning personal assistants, financial, and legal domains, etc. While these systems can substantially improve productivity and service quality, effective agency typically requires access to sensitive personal or organizational information. However, this access introduces critical inference-time privacy risks, specifically regarding contextually appropriate information disclosure. While recent studies highlight the inability of agentic LLMs to consistently adhere to privacy norms, existing defenses often rely on auxiliary LLM-based monitors. However, these defenses are expensive and offer limited protection against attacks that are robust to semantic censorship. To contrast this background, this paper proposes a notion of privacy filters based on activation

translated_title: NeuroFilter：面向隐私敏感型大语言模型智能体的基于激活的防护栏
translated_abstract: 智能体化大语言模型（LLM）是能够在非结构化数据上进行推理、规划和执行工具调用的模型。这些能力使其在个人助理、金融和法律等领域能够实现变革性的应用。虽然这些系统能够显著提升生产力和服务质量，但有效的智能体行为通常需要访问敏感的个人或组织信息。然而，这种访问会引入关键的推理阶段隐私风险，尤其是关于如何在特定情境下恰当披露信息的问题。尽管近期的研究指出智能体化LLM难以持续遵守隐私规范，现有的防御方法往往依赖于辅助性的基于LLM的监控器。然而，这类防御方法成本高昂，且对于能够绕过语义审查的攻击所提供的保护有限。针对这一背景，本文提出了一种基于激活的隐私过滤器概念
tldr: 本文提出NeuroFilter，一种基于大语言模型内部激活而非昂贵的辅助LLM监控器的隐私过滤器，用于在推理阶段防止智能体不当披露敏感信息，并能有效防御对语义审查具有鲁棒性的攻击。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes NeuroFilter, an activation-based privacy filter for LLM agents that leverages internal activations rather than costly auxiliary LLM monitors to prevent inappropriate disclosure of sensitive information at inference time and defend against attacks robust to semantic censorship.
